tone_patterns: Neutral, analytical tone focused on describing impacts, risks, and opportunities without promotional language
Uses cause–effect phrasing to connect an issue to business and stakeholder outcomes
Balances positive and negative framing to demonstrate completeness and avoid one-sided narratives
Employs risk-aware language (e.g., conditionality and likelihood) to distinguish actual vs potential effects
paragraph_patterns: Content is presented primarily as compact, label-led entries rather than long narrative paragraphs
Each entry follows a consistent micro-structure: topic label + brief explanation of mechanism + resulting consequence(s)
Multi-consequence statements are chained in a single entry (operational + financial + legal + reputational) to show breadth
Uses short, scannable text blocks with line breaks to fit within table cells and maintain readability
heading_patterns: Section header at top of page followed by a thematic subtopic title that includes an ordinal number and topic name
Subtopic titles are repeated as page-level identifiers (e.g., 'Strategy' plus numbered topic) to reinforce navigation
Uses clear, taxonomy-like headings that mirror IFRS-style disclosure categories (impact materiality vs financial materiality)
table_patterns: Two-part tabular structure per topic: (1) Impact materiality table and (2) Financial materiality table
Impact materiality table uses four main columns: positive impacts, actual/potential flag, negative impacts, actual/potential flag
Financial materiality table uses four main columns: risks, timeframe, opportunities, timeframe
Entries begin with a bold/lead-in label (concept name) followed by a colon and explanatory text within the same cell
Time horizons are standardized into discrete buckets (e.g., short/medium/long and combinations) and repeated consistently
Tables prioritize comparability: same column order, same labeling, and similar row density across topics
Cells accommodate wrapped text; long descriptions are allowed but kept concise and structured
Positive/negative and risk/opportunity are presented side-by-side to encourage balanced reading
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No charts or graphics used in the excerpt; the design relies on structured tables as the primary visual device
Visual hierarchy is achieved through table headers, column grouping, and consistent typographic emphasis rather than diagrams
pdf_layout_patterns: Each topic spans a dedicated page with consistent header/footer elements for navigation and citation
Page includes a prominent section label ('Strategy') and a numbered topic title near the bottom or header area for continuity
Tables occupy the majority of the page area, suggesting a grid-based layout optimized for scanning
Consistent pagination and report identifier/footer line appear on each page to support referencing
Whitespace is managed to keep tables readable; text wraps within fixed column widths rather than expanding layout
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses IFRS-aligned categorization language: 'Impact Materiality' and 'Financial Materiality' as organizing constructs
Explicitly distinguishes 'Actual' versus 'Potential' impacts to clarify status and uncertainty
Separates 'Risks' and 'Opportunities' and assigns a 'Timeframe' to each to support decision-useful disclosure
Uses non-absolute wording for forward-looking items (e.g., may/could/likely-style conditional framing) to avoid overcommitment
Includes multiple impact dimensions (customers, employees, operations, compliance, reputation) to demonstrate completeness
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented as structured assertions rather than quantified metrics in this excerpt
Credibility is supported through specificity of pathways (how an issue leads to outcomes) rather than data points
Uses consistent classification tags (actual/potential; timeframe) as a quasi-evidentiary scaffold for comparability
Mentions typical consequence categories (financial loss, legal exposure, operational disruption, reputational effects) to ground statements
section_specific_observations: The Strategy section operationalizes materiality by mapping impacts and financial effects in parallel, topic-by-topic
Numbered topics imply a repeatable template that can be applied across multiple sustainability themes
The layout emphasizes decision-usefulness: quick identification of what matters, direction of effect, and when it may materialize
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organization name or references to being a specific type of institution
Any topic-specific claims that imply performance, leadership, or superiority
Any sector-specific examples that could be interpreted as factual statements about the new company
Any mention of particular regulations, jurisdictions, or compliance regimes as if they apply universally
Any detailed consequence chains that mirror the reference too closely in wording or ordering
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Company name and report title references
Specific topic labels and numbered topic titles tied to the reference company’s materiality list
Any implied claims about robustness, leadership positioning, or competitiveness as factual attributes
Any mention of particular stakeholder groups or outcomes framed in a way that could be company-specific
Any references to specific climate event examples or sector exposures presented as the company’s realities
